findings.title: Samples used to establish or disprove a requirement lie inside the requested window

cases.case: Kalman filter, record ends at t = 3.5 s (samples t = 0..3 s), mean-square-error level 0.616808

result.explanation: the optimal (time-varying) Kalman filter attains the minimum mean-square error over any estimator of the same data under the stated model (mmse) at every sample; its error variance at every sample from t = 0 s to the end of the record t = 3.5 s reaches 0.617722 > 0.616808, so any estimator exceeds the requested level at that sample as well
result.impossibility: the optimal (time-varying) Kalman filter attains the minimum mean-square error over any estimator of the same data under the stated model (mmse) at every sample; its error variance at every sample from t = 0 s to the end of the record t = 3.5 s reaches 0.617722 > 0.616808, so any estimator exceeds the requested level at that sample as well

cases.case: observer, velocity error <= 0.075 rad/s on the record from 0.05 s to its end at 0.06 s

result.claim: |error| <= 0.0566298 at every sample instant t_k >= 0.05 s for every admissible initial error, measurement error and disturbance

cases.case: 100 Hz encoder, requirement on t in [0.01 s, 0.0165 s]; the two-signal argument needs a sample at or after 0.01633 s

result.explanation: no causal estimator of the velocity can guarantee a worst-case error below 2 sqrt(D V) = 0.0489898 at times t >= 4 sqrt(V/D) = 0.0163299 s when the unmodelled acceleration may be any signal bounded by 6 and |v| <= 0.0001 (two admissible signals with identical measurements whose velocities differ by 4 sqrt(D V); the stated velocity range admits them and the requirement applies at such times)
result.impossibility: no causal estimator of the velocity can guarantee a worst-case error below 2 sqrt(D V) = 0.0489898 at times t >= 4 sqrt(V/D) = 0.0163299 s when the unmodelled acceleration may be any signal bounded by 6 and |v| <= 0.0001 (two admissible signals with identical measurements whose velocities differ by 4 sqrt(D V); the stated velocity range admits them and the requirement applies at such times)

findings.title: Kalman filter start-up: estimate, exported covariance and explanation agree

cases.case: scalar random walk, Q = R = 1, P0 = 100, constant (steady-state) gain

result.claim: constant (steady-state) Kalman gain: in the limit k -> infinity its error covariance equals that of the optimal filter, whose estimate is the conditional mean of the state given the measurements and inputs; minimum mean-square error among all estimators measurable with respect to the same information (jointly Gaussian initial state and noises); at finite times the time-varying filter is better (horizon 'finite'); error variance of the target in steady state (the limit as k -> infinity): at most 0.618034
result.uncertainty_type: error covariance (second-order statistic); not a deterministic error bound

findings.title: The decision uses all supplied constraints together

cases.case: total disturbance bound D = 6 and, for the exactly known model, additive bound d = 1.5; ultimate velocity limit 0.045 rad/s (two-signal limits 2 sqrt(DV) = 0.0490, 2 sqrt(dV) = 0.0245)

result.explanation: no causal estimator of the velocity can guarantee a worst-case error below 2 sqrt(D V) = 0.0489898 at times t >= 4 sqrt(V/D) = 0.0163299 s when the unmodelled acceleration may be any signal bounded by 6 and |v| <= 0.0001 (two admissible signals with identical measurements whose velocities differ by 4 sqrt(D V); the stated velocity range admits them and the requirement applies at such times)
result.impossibility: no causal estimator of the velocity can guarantee a worst-case error below 2 sqrt(D V) = 0.0489898 at times t >= 4 sqrt(V/D) = 0.0163299 s when the unmodelled acceleration may be any signal bounded by 6 and |v| <= 0.0001 (two admissible signals with identical measurements whose velocities differ by 4 sqrt(D V); the stated velocity range admits them and the requirement applies at such times)

cases.case: smallest mean-square error of the speed; nominal input gain b = 4 but the true value lies in [3.6, 4.4]

result.claim: constant (steady-state) Kalman gain: in the limit k -> infinity its error covariance equals that of the optimal filter, whose estimate is the minimum mean-square error among linear (affine) estimators of the same measurements and inputs (only means and covariances are assumed; no claim against nonlinear estimators); at finite times the time-varying filter is better (horizon 'finite'); error variance of the target in steady state (the limit as k -> infinity): at most 6.34109e-05

findings.title: A worst-case limit does not show that a probability requirement is impossible

cases.case: speed error within 0.04 rad/s with probability 0.9 (bounded noise; worst-case limit 2 sqrt(DV) = 0.049)

result.claim: in steady state (the limit as k -> infinity), |error| <= 0.04 with probability at least 0.960368 (Chebyshev inequality with error variance P (distribution-free): P(|e| <= r) >= 1 - P / r^2); the statement is per time instant, not simultaneous over the window

result.impossibility: no causal estimator of the velocity can guarantee a worst-case error below 2 sqrt(D V) = 0.0489898 at times t >= 4 sqrt(V/D) = 0.0163299 s when the unmodelled acceleration may be any signal bounded by 6 and |v| <= 0.0001 (two admissible signals with identical measurements whose velocities differ by 4 sqrt(D V); the stated velocity range admits them and the requirement applies at such times)
